_comment: One tile, the whole network (23 IR ops, 21260642 MACs). @generated by phase1_bindings.py from the board's own compose verdicts (results/phase1_compose.json) — a lane appears here only if qnn-context-binary-generator returned rc=0 for it on this board. Model is modelblaster.models.dronet_sg from the zoo at /scratch/dima/rose-infra/RoSE/soc/sw/xpu-rt/zephyr-chipyard-sw/modelblaster, exported to ONNX at opset 17 and converted with snpe-onnx-to-dlc; the int8 lanes come from the qairt-quantizer output over 10 seeded synthetic calibration samples.
_scaled_variant_note: dronet and mlp_control non-default rungs keep SEEDED RANDOM INIT — the trained checkpoint only fits the default geometry — so they are valid latency and scheduling targets and must never be quoted as an accuracy result. yolov8_nano rungs are the exception: channel counts are input-size independent, so get_model() loads the COCO checkpoint at every rung. fastdepth has no committed checkpoint at all and is always seeded-random.
_rewrite_note: Lane(s) ['hta', 'dsp', 'cpu'] come from the rewritten variant dronet_sg_hta (chain ['onnxsim', 'bn_to_mul_add', 'flatten_gemm_to_conv'], NUMERICS-PRESERVING), adopted because it measured better on that lane. HTA rejects Batchnorm; dronet's BNs follow the residual Add so there is nothing to fold them into, and the Flatten before the two heads is what the converter turns into the Transpose HTA also rejects.
_precision_note: The CPU lane's precision is chosen per tile on measured evidence, not per network: cpu=fp32, dsp=int8, gpu=fp16, hta=int8
